Definition: from G4642; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn:--harden.
BiblicalUsage: Skleruno means to harden, to make stubborn, and it is used of men and of God alike. The Jews in Ephesus were hardened and believed not, the writer to the Hebrews warns daily lest any be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin, and Paul says God has mercy on whom He will and hardens whom He will.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hardening is the end of a road, not the beginning of one. Sin deceives, the heart stiffens, and I hold that today, while it is called today, is the day to hear His voice.
